QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_26

question.text: In Theory of Change design, 'reverse logic' (working backwards) typically means:

answer.text: Starting with the stated long-term impact and working backwards through outcomes, outputs, activities, to inputs — testing at each step whether the lower-level element is NECESSARY and SUFFICIENT to produce the next
Writing the LFA in reverse alphabetical order
Submitting the AIR before fieldwork begins

explanation.text: The Logic: Reverse logic starts with the intended long-term impact and traces backwards through outcomes -> outputs -> activities -> inputs, asking at each step: 'Is this lower element NECESSARY and SUFFICIENT to produce the next element?' This diagnostic is more rigorous than forward logic because it surfaces orphan activities (producing no needed output) and missing prerequisites. The Trap: B, C, D are nonsense distractors. Cross-Exam Context: Reverse-logic testing is used in SAS engagement planning (XXIII Ch 7) and parallels control-objective mapping in statutory/internal audit. Assessor's Pro-Tip: On every engagement, run a reverse-logic pass on one outcome chain. If you find an activity with no upward connection to any needed output, either the LFA is broken or the SE is running redundant work. Both are findings worth reporting.
